items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: Frankie Newton was the leader, and Sammy Benskon was the pianist and me who worked there for a while.

ctx.x: Eddie Barefield, yeah, Eddie and I've been associated for I don't know how long. We used to live near one another, and he'd have to pass where I was staying in order to get to the subway or whatever. And Tom Waley lived across the street, who was Duke's copyist, and Eddie Heywood lived in that building, and Pete Brown, the terrific alto man, was in that area.

And we used to -- and I was staying with a tenor player by the name of Lem Johnson. He and I lived together after I was separated from my first wife. And these guys would pass by the house -- Frankie Newton -- and we'd have jam session every day.
And then Flip started coming by, Flip -- Jazz at the Philharmonic --
